title: CallLint agent discovery index (v1)
description:
The single entry point an agent fetches to enumerate every distribution surface CallLint tracks. Generated from apps/web/data/distribution-surfaces.json by scripts/generate-distribution-surfaces.mjs; never hand-edited.

Each surface's `type` is DERIVED from which SSOT container holds the record, so it cannot disagree with the SSOT's own shape. `status` is the human-facing public label; the internal support enum travels separately in `supportClass` and only for records that have one.

This surface carries distribution facts only. It deliberately contains no risk, popularity, demand or SEO score: distribution channel is orthogonal to a security verdict, and a consumer must not be able to derive a verdict from where a server was found.

schemaVersion.description: Contract identifier. Distinct from the Safe-install bake's `calllint.discovery.v1` in .well-known/calllint.json, which is a different document with a different owner — do not merge the two.

canonical.description: This document is the canonical discovery root (§4's ONE layer). Published as a field rather than left implicit because two machine surfaces exist — this one and `agent-surfaces.json` — and a consumer that finds either first must be able to tell which is the root. Both are generated projections of the same SSOT, so they cannot disagree on a shared fact; `agent-surfaces.json` carries the reciprocal `canonicalIndex` pointer back to this file. Neither is a second source of truth.

describes.description: What release this index describes. Deliberately not a wall-clock stamp — a timestamp makes every generator run produce a diff even when no fact changed, which would destroy `--check`'s ability to distinguish drift from noise.

surfaceTypes.description: The closed §6 vocabulary, published so a consumer can tell an unpopulated type from an unknown one. `marketplace` and `mirror` are expected to have zero members today: CallLint distributes through no marketplace and operates no mirror. A truthful empty set, not an omission.

counts.description: Denominators, published so a consumer that reads zero surfaces can tell an empty index from a failed fetch.

coverage.description:
§6's Agent Adoption Coverage Index: the OBLIGATION beside the fact. `counts` above says how many records exist; a consumer reading `agent-harness: 18` cannot tell a complete cohort from one that silently lost a host. Each tier therefore publishes `required` (counted from the SSOT's `coverageTier` field) next to `present` (counted from this document's own surfaces), so a dropped host moves the two apart instead of shrinking one unchecked number.

COVERAGE MEANS A RECORD EXISTS. It never means the host is supported, and never that its support is good. new19 §9: "Do not claim implementation where none exists. The record may honestly say: DISCOVERY_ONLY." That is why each tier carries a `bySupportClass` histogram rather than a verified/unverified flag — tier0 is fully covered while only 2 of its 5 entries are NATIVE, and any boolean would have to round that into a support claim manufactured by a coverage requirement.

byTier.description: A total partition of the host cohort. `beyond-section-9` is a first-class tier, not a leftover bucket: CallLint covers hosts new19 never named, and that growth must be named rather than inferred from absence.

required.description: How many host records this tier obliges CallLint to hold. `minimum: 1` because an empty tier would make its coverage claim vacuously true — 0/0 is not evidence of coverage.

present.description: How many of them actually reached this document's `surfaces` array. Counted independently of `required` so the two can disagree; the generator refuses to publish when they do.

hosts.description: Named, not just counted. A count alone cannot tell a reviewer WHICH host left a tier, and that is the edit worth reviewing.

bySupportClass.description: The honest shape of the tier: how its records split across the support ontology. Deliberately a histogram and not a verified/unverified boolean — see this schema's `coverage` description. Keys are the internal support enum, which this document already publishes in the `supportClass` field; §20's ban on internal tokens scopes to the human-facing `status` label, not to explicitly-named enum fields.

allOf.description: §5's richer fields are REQUIRED for an agent-harness and absent elsewhere, rather than emitted empty for every surface. An mcp-registry has no `capabilities` and a search-surface has no `discovery` config path; writing `[]` there would state a measured emptiness that was never measured. Same precedent as `supportClass`, which this schema already scopes to records that have one. A harness is exactly where §5's contract has to hold, so for that type it is enforced, not optional.

status.description: Human-facing state. For an agent-harness this is the public support label (Auto-detects / Scan config / Guide only) and never the internal enum, which §20 keeps off human-readable surfaces. For a registry it is the listing state; for a candidate feed it is the feed's role, since §86 forbids a feed from implying support.

supportClass.description: The internal support ontology, present only on records that have one (today: agent-harness). An agent consuming a contract wants the enum; the four classes ARE the contract.

describedBy.description: Where the per-surface detail lives. Deliberately the same canonical host page rather than a second `/agents/<id>` page set: commit 79f3cb8 deleted the model x harness cartesian plane, and a second page per surface would rebuild it. `/agents/<id>` exists only as a 301 alias into this URL.

capabilities.description: The authority surfaces this harness exposes to an agent — what it can reach, not what CallLint supports. Projected from the SSOT's `authoritySurfaces`; this is the field §5 names `capabilities`.

calllintSupport.description: What CallLint can actually do here, kept structurally separate from `capabilities` so a reader can never mistake the host's authority for CallLint's coverage. `commands` is empty exactly when no truthful command exists (§7: never claim an implementation that is absent) — an empty array here is a measured emptiness, unlike an absent field.

distribution.description: How CallLint reaches this harness. `state` carries the public label, never the internal pipeline enum, for the same §20 reason `status` does.

discovery.description: How an agent or CallLint finds this harness's configuration. `configPaths` is the evidence CallLint reads; `autoDetected` is true only for NATIVE, so a consumer can branch without re-deriving the support ontology.

officialSources.description: First-party vendor URLs. Required on EVERY surface type: §7 forbids upgrading a state without evidence, and this is where the evidence for a surface's existence is cited. Measured present on 18/18 hosts before being made required.
